tema: Reviews the potential role of the different components of the immune system in the pathogenesis of ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative review; no own population.
hallazgos: Points to alterations of NK cell function compatible with an infectious onset, inconsistent cytokine data although more robust in recent large cohorts, and possible clinical improvements with B cell depletion therapies.
conclusion: Heterogeneity and the day-to-day variability of symptoms and mediators explain the lack of consensus; longitudinal studies, defined hypotheses, replication in different cohorts and stratification are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions (from the discussion) prioritize hypothesis-driven studies over the search for biomarkers, a nuance not explicit in the abstract.

tema: Studies the frequency of CFS, sleep disturbances and quality of life in mothers of children with cerebral palsy according to the child's functional level.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in caregiver mothers with the Chalder Fatigue Scale, FSS, PSQI and SF-12, and the child's functional scales (GMFCS, MACS, CFCS, EDACS); canonical correlation analysis.
hallazgos: 80.4% of the mothers met CDC-1994 criteria for CFS (n = 45); housewives had more fatigue and worse mental health; the canonical correlation was 0.815, with the child's manual ability (MACS) as the variable with the greatest effect.
conclusion: The frequency of CFS is very high in these mothers; maternal employment status and the child's manual ability are the most important factors; they propose employment measures and rehabilitation focused on manual skills.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add social recommendations. It should be noted that CFS is defined by questionnaire in caregivers, not by clinical diagnosis.

tema: To explore alterations in the composition and function of the oral microbiome in Han Chinese patients with CFS.
diseno: Case-control with 16S rRNA gene sequencing and functional prediction with PICRUSt. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Alpha diversity showed no differences, but overall composition differed (p < 0.01); more Fusobacteria, Leptotrichia, Prevotella and Fusobacterium, and fewer Haemophilus, Veillonella and Porphyromonas; amino acid and energy pathways were implicated.
conclusion: The oral microbiome differs in a minor but significant way, with implications for pathogenesis, diagnosis and treatment.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions describe the differences as minor, a more cautious nuance than the abstract.

tema: Reviews advances and possibilities in the diagnosis, pathophysiology and care of CFS.
diseno: Narrative review; no own population.
hallazgos: CFS affects ~1 in 100 primary care patients; clinical diagnosis requires recognizing typical fatigue, excluding other causes and few tests; acute infections trigger a significant minority of cases and the evidence points to functional brain changes and a genetic contribution.
conclusion: Studies have ruled out ongoing infection, immunological or endocrine disorder, primary sleep disorder or a purely psychiatric cause; functional neuroimaging and a large GWAS are needed, and diagnosis and care should be improved through training.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; no conclusions are available. Its stance that it is not an immunological disorder contrasts with other works on this topic.

tema: Position paper from the Oslo Chronic Fatigue Consortium that challenges the narrative of incurability of chronic fatigue syndromes and long COVID.
diseno: Opinion/position article based on previous research; no own empirical data.
hallazgos: They propose that symptoms reflect the brain's response to biological, psychological and social factors (sustained activation of the stress response) and that they persist if perceived as threatening and activities are avoided.
conclusion: Recovery would often be possible through a less threatening understanding of symptoms and a gradual return to activity; they call for a more open dialogue that includes recovered patients.
triangulacion: Keywords (threat perception, avoidance behaviour, recovery) and abstract are consistent; the conclusions text is almost only the conflict-of-interest statement (CBT royalties, Lightning Process, etc.), which adds no content but contextualizes the stance.

tema: Proposes a common pathobiological model for post-COVID-19 syndrome and ME/CFS based on chronic inflammation, neuroglial dysfunction and plasmalogen deficiency.
diseno: Review and theoretical hypothesis; no own population.
hallazgos: Points out that both conditions share fatigue, brain fog, PEM and autonomic dysfunction; plasmalogen reduction has been described in ME/CFS and acute COVID-19, associated with severity, but has not been studied in post-COVID.
conclusion: Plasmalogen replacement therapy, combined with nutraceuticals and lifestyle interventions, could relieve symptoms; preclinical and translational research is required.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with funding noise) are consistent; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious in calling for preclinical research, whereas the abstract describes the therapy as simple, effective and safe.

tema: Communication proposing extracorporeal apheresis as a therapeutic option in post-COVID-19 syndrome and autoantibody-mediated ME/CFS.
diseno: Short opinion article with own data not detailed; sample size and methods not stated.
hallazgos: Similar elevations of autoantibodies against β-adrenergic and muscarinic receptors were observed in both groups; apheresis with a special filter appears to reduce these antibodies and improve symptoms in CFS.
conclusion: Neuroapheresis could be a promising option for post-COVID; an app is proposed to recruit and monitor patients in future trials.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the extracted conclusions are mostly acknowledgements and licence text, apart from the app proposal. Evidence of efficacy is not detailed in the sources.

tema: Reviews studies on viral agents associated with ME/CFS and proposes strategies for designing better studies.
diseno: Literature review; no own population.
hallazgos: The evidence on chronic viral infection is controversial and limited by small studies and non-validated designs, although it points to viral involvement in at least a subgroup.
conclusion: Recommends assessing markers of viral activity in early phases, longitudinal studies, comparison with other comorbidities, subtyping, quantitative viral load assays, additional biological samples and functional studies.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are more concrete than the abstract in providing a detailed list of methodological strategies.

tema: Explores circadian rhythm patterns of activity-rest and distal skin temperature and their relationship to symptoms in ME/CFS, in winter and summer.
diseno: Case-control study with 10 women with CFS/ME (Fukuda and 2003 Canadian criteria) and 10 matched controls; 7-day ActTrust actigraphy (activity, distal skin temperature, light), sleep diary, questionnaires and spectral analysis; recordings in winter and summer.
hallazgos: There were no differences in rhythm stability, sleep latency or awakenings, but daily activity, relative amplitude and stability of the activity rhythm were lower in patients. Nocturnal distal skin temperature was lower only in winter, and the 12-h second harmonic differed between groups and correlated with the clinical picture.
conclusion: Circadian regulation and cutaneous vasodilator responses may play a role in ME/CFS; more actigraphic studies are needed, including severe patients.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions broaden the focus toward circadian metabolomics and possible biomarkers, beyond what the data show.

tema: Reviews circadian rhythm disruption in ME/CFS and its implications for the post-acute sequelae of COVID-19.
diseno: Narrative review with hypothesis proposal; no own population.
hallazgos: The evidence suggests circadian misalignment or greater variability rather than total loss, with peripheral rhythms (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure) more affected than central ones; TGF-β, elevated in ME/CFS, synchronizes peripheral clocks.
conclusion: Altered TGF-β signalling could disorganize physiological rhythms; if validated, circadian rhythms would be a target to prevent or reverse the progression from PASC to ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the circadian-TGF-β-PASC axis; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious in making the therapeutic relevance conditional on validation.

tema: Analyses the relationship between orthostatic autonomic responses, circadian variations in skin temperature and endothelial biomarkers in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 67 women with ME/CFS and 48 matched controls; autonomic questionnaires; orthostatic test with blood pressure, heart rate and wrist temperature; one-week actigraphy; circulating endothelial biomarkers.
hallazgos: Patients showed higher resting blood pressure and heart rate and greater amplitude of the activity rhythm. ET-1 and VCAM-1 were elevated, and ET-1 was associated with the stability and amplitude of the temperature rhythm and with the self-reported questionnaires.
conclusion: Circadian and haemodynamic alterations are associated with endothelial dysfunction and support dysautonomia in ME/CFS; more research on vascular tone as a possible therapeutic target is needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and reinforce one another on the dysautonomia-circadian rhythm-endothelin-1 axis; the PDF conclusions highlight the novelty of linking the autonomic nervous system with vasoconstriction/vasodilation.

tema: Systematic review protocol to assess circulating leptin levels in ME/CFS or fibromyalgia compared with healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review protocol (PRISMA, JBI methodology) of observational studies in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Science Direct and PsycINFO; meta-analysis with JBI SUMARI and GRADE. PROSPERO registration CRD42020169903.
hallazgos: Not applicable (protocol without results).
conclusion: Not stated; the final text describes the planned synthesis (random-effects models, I2 heterogeneity, GRADE) and a possible limitation due to lack of measurement details.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the conclusions (from the discussion) are methodological, consistent with a protocol but with no findings to triangulate.

tema: Examines ocular symptoms and signs of dry eye in Gulf War veterans with ME/CFS.
diseno: Prospective cross-sectional study of 124 veterans: ME/CFS (n = 32), intermediate fatigue (n = 48) and controls (n = 44) according to Canadian Criteria; ocular questionnaires, slit lamp and inflammatory markers in blood.
hallazgos: Dry eye symptoms (OSDI 48.9 vs 38.8 vs 19.1; p < 0.001) and ocular pain symptoms (NPSI-E 23.0 vs 19.8 vs 6.5) were greater in ME/CFS and intermediate fatigue, whereas ocular surface parameters and inflammatory markers were similar.
conclusion: People with ME/CFS report more ocular pain with similar signs of dry eye, suggesting mechanisms beyond the ocular surface.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the structured abstract and agree with it; the keywords reflect the ocular focus and the veteran population well.

tema: Describes the clinical profile and differential diagnosis aspects of ME/CFS patients in Riga (Latvia).
diseno: Observational study in 65 Caucasian outpatients; questionnaires, specialist evaluation and visual analogue scale (VAS).
hallazgos: ME/CFS with comorbidities was associated with greater severity; fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia and sleep disorders were more prevalent than in patients without ME/CFS; VAS tended to decrease with age and duration of fatigue.
conclusion: Comorbidities are associated with a more severe course and NSAIDs are the most used drug group to reduce symptoms; larger samples are needed to better differentiate ME/CFS from other fatigue conditions.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are more cautious in acknowledging the small sample size and add sex differences not mentioned in the abstract.

tema: Characterizes CFS patients with POTS and differentiates them from CFS patients without POTS.
diseno: Study in 179 CFS patients (CDC 1994 criteria) from a specialist clinical service; fatigue, sleepiness (ESS), orthostatic (OGS) and HADS scales, heart rate variability and haemodynamic response to standing.
hallazgos: 13% (24) had POTS; they were younger, less fatigued, less depressed and had less daytime sleepiness, but greater OI and autonomic dysfunction. The combination ESS ≤9 and OGS ≥9 identified patients with POTS with predictive values of 100%.
conclusion: POTS defines a distinct clinical subgroup within CFS, identifiable with validated clinical tools, which could guide additional studies and heart rate control treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (taken from the abstract) are consistent; all three highlight the POTS subgroup, autonomic dysfunction and daytime sleepiness as a differentiating feature.

tema: Describes the clinical characteristics of patients with unexplained hypothalamic disorder diagnosed by the CRH stimulation test, with the aim of clarifying its pathophysiology.
diseno: Retrospective study of patients undergoing the CRH test, classified into four groups: normal response (n = 18), unexplained hypothalamic disorder (n = 18), explainable (n = 38) and pituitary disorder (n = 15); comparison of clinical characteristics, insulin tolerance test and urinary cortisol.
hallazgos: The unexplained hypothalamic disorder group showed lower ACTH peaks than the normal group, attenuated diurnal variation and urinary free cortisol in the normal-low range; they were mostly young women with chronic fatigue. Hydrocortisone at physiological doses reduced fatigue only in some patients.
conclusion: These patients show HPA axis dysfunction and some a mild central adrenal insufficiency; the partial response to hydrocortisone suggests that the dysfunction could be a physiological adaptation, relevant for understanding ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent: the keywords (HPA axis, secondary adrenal insufficiency, hydrocortisone) match the abstract and PDF conclusions, which reproduce the abstract's conclusion almost word for word. The link with ME/CFS is interpretive and is raised as a future line.

tema: Interdisciplinary clinical guideline for the management of ME/CFS, long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions (IACC).
diseno: Clinical guideline prepared by clinicians, researchers and experts with lived experience; no sample.
hallazgos: Includes chapters on caregiver support and disability documentation: recording fluctuations, PEM episodes, hours of upright activity (HUA) and objective tests of orthostatic intolerance.
conclusion: Supporting the caregiver is a central part of person-centred care, and clinicians have a critical role in documenting and advocating for functional limitations for accommodations and benefits.
triangulacion: There are no keywords; the abstract is opening text (acknowledgements and authors) and the conclusions are fragments from specific chapters (care and disability), so they only partially cover the guideline. Both texts agree on the compassionate, patient-centred approach.

tema: Determines whether cognitive impairment persists after completing a tilt test in adults with ME/CFS.
diseno: Study in 128 consecutive patients with ME/CFS and OI; N-back tests (2-back and 3-back) before and in the 5 min after a 30-min tilt test.
hallazgos: After the test, correct responses fell from 77% to 62% (2-back) and from 57% to 41% (3-back), and reaction times increased (p<0.0001). There were no differences by severity, comorbid fibromyalgia or presence of POTS.
conclusion: Working memory remains impaired after orthostatic stress in ME/CFS, which agrees with PEM being able to start immediately after orthostatic stress.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on OI, cognitive impairment and working memory; the conclusions add the connection with PEM, not mentioned in the keywords or abstract.

tema: Reviews the overlaps between ME/CFS and cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and asks whether both reflect a stress-induced phenotypic instability.
diseno: Narrative literature review on shared mechanisms (HPA axis, serotonergic system, cytokines and inflammation, metabolic and mitochondrial insufficiency, genetic changes) and stressors such as ionizing radiation.
hallazgos: Common candidate mechanisms are identified: neurological dysfunction, changes in serotonin and the circadian clock, elevated inflammation, metabolic deficits and genetic changes. The authors propose that CRF and ME/CFS could lie on a continuum of biological responses to stress modulated by genetic predisposition.
conclusion: There is notable symptom overlap and some evidence of an aetiological link, but the role of radiation dose remains unclear; common biomarkers need to be identified to guide therapies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on the mechanistic axes (HPA, serotonin, mitochondria, radiation). The conclusions are more cautious than the continuum hypothesis, stressing the lack of evidence on radiation, especially in ME/CFS.

tema: Compares plasma extracellular vesicles from patients with mild and severe ME/CFS with those of healthy controls, as a possible biomarker.
diseno: Case-control study with flow cytometry to type the cellular origin of the vesicles using surface markers. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Severe ME/CFS correlated with more vesicles carrying the B lymphocyte marker CD19 and the platelet marker CD41a, although the difference ceased to be significant after correcting for multiple comparisons.
conclusion: There could be a dysregulation of B lymphocyte and platelet activation or homeostasis, which must be validated in a replication cohort.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on vesicles, severity and CD19. The conclusions (discussion) relate the finding to cytokine profiles and low NK function, and maintain the abstract's caution; the rest is administrative noise.

tema: Compares the response to a two-day CPET between women with ME/CFS and women with idiopathic chronic fatigue (ICF).
diseno: Comparative study with 51 women with ICF and 50 age-matched women with ME/CFS; VO2, heart rate, blood pressure, workload and RER at peak and ventilatory threshold.
hallazgos: ME/CFS patients worsened on the second CPET (VO2 and workload at peak and ventilatory threshold), whereas ICF patients improved with no significant change in peak workload; resting heart rate and RER did not change.
conclusion: The reduction in exercise capacity on the second CPET is confirmed in women with ME/CFS; ICF responds like sedentary controls, suggesting a different and possibly trainable disease.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. Minor discrepancy: the abstract mentions a male population although women were studied; the conclusions go further in suggesting that ICF would be trainable and ME/CFS would not.

tema: Compares T cell receptor (TCR) diversity between people with ME and controls to test the autoimmune hypothesis.
diseno: Case-control study with sequencing of the TCR α/δ, β and γ loci in 40 samples per group (severe ME, mild or moderate ME, multiple sclerosis and healthy controls) from the UK ME/CFS Biobank; classification with machine learning (P-SVM).
hallazgos: The method, effective with simulated data, failed to separate the samples into the four groups in a statistically significant way.
conclusion: The results do not support the idea that the blood of people with ME frequently contains altered TCR diversity.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (TCR repertoire, autoimmune hypothesis, multiple sclerosis), and the abstract presents a negative result. The conclusions text (discussion) is noise (acknowledgements, funding, data availability).

tema: Compares a 20-degree versus a 70-degree tilt test in adolescents with ME/CFS to assess the reduction in cerebral blood flow and the detection of POTS.
diseno: Analysis of 83 studies in adolescents with ME/CFS (42 at 20 degrees, 41 at 70 degrees; 17 with both); extracranial Doppler of the internal carotid and vertebral arteries.
hallazgos: At 20 degrees no patient developed POTS versus 32% at 70 degrees (p=0.0002). The CBF reduction was 27% at 20 degrees and 31% at 70 degrees.
conclusion: A 20-degree test provokes in young people a CBF reduction comparable to that of adults at 70 degrees without inducing syncope, but detects less POTS, so 70 degrees is required for that diagnosis.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions also stress the absence of syncope and the false positives at 70 degrees, while the abstract calls for more studies to use CBF as a classification standard.

tema: Compares the fatigue scores obtained with the Korean version of the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-K) and the modified Chalder fatigue scale (mKCFQ).
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 70 participants (40 men, 30 women; median age 48 years) from university staff, grouped by self-reported fatigue (mild 20, moderate 42, severe 8); correlation analysis and multidimensional scaling (MDS).
hallazgos: Total scores correlated significantly (r = 75%), with higher correlation in general fatigue (79%) and physical fatigue (66%) than in motivation (41%) and activity (26%, not significant). The MFI-K overestimated fatigue, especially in the mild group, and the mKCFQ better discriminated the severity groups.
conclusion: Both instruments are useful, especially for physical fatigue; the MFI-K could serve in moderate-severe fatigue such as that of CFS and the mKCFQ across the whole spectrum, including sub-healthy subjects.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the high correlation and on the better discrimination of the mKCFQ. The PDF conclusions add the need to improve the activity and motivation dimensions; the keywords mention neither the Chalder scale nor CFS, which is only a context of application.

tema: To compare serum acylcarnitine levels between patients with ME/CFS/SEID and healthy controls.
diseno: PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis in PubMed and Ichushi-Web; 276 records, 7 studies, 403 patients.
hallazgos: Patients had significantly lower serum acylcarnitine, with high statistical heterogeneity.
conclusion: Serum acylcarnitine, together with symptoms, could be a useful and minimally invasive diagnostic tool.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions do not mention the high heterogeneity. The keywords are generic (biomarkers) and do not name acylcarnitine.
